A 39-year-old Caucasian man was referred for evaluation of severe rod–cone retinal dystrophy. He had no history of parental consanguinity. Since childhood he noted high bilateral myopia and nyctalopia; he underwent uneventful bilateral cataract extraction with 13D monofocal intraocular lenses 3 years earlier. His medical history was notable for moderate intellectual disability, transient neutropenia in childhood that resolved spontaneously, microcephaly, truncal obesity, and joint hyperextensibility of the hands, feet, ankles, and knees. He had appropriate social behavior despite intellectual disability. On examination, his facial features included a thick head of hair, bushy eyebrows, a short upturned philtrum, a high nasal bridge with a beak-shaped nose, and an ogival palate. 

Best-corrected visual acuity was 2/10 in each eye. Slit-lamp examination and intraocular pressure were normal. Fundus examination showed bilateral disc pallor, generalized arteriolar narrowing, mid-peripheral “bone-spicule” pigmentary changes, and retinal pigment epithelium atrophy. Macular optical coherence tomography demonstrated diffuse RPE and outer retinal atrophy involving the subfoveal region without cystoid macular edema. Peripapillary OCT revealed chorioretinal thinning with decreased retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (global RNFL thickness of 53 μm in the right eye and 75 μm in the left eye). Fluorescein angiography showed diffuse RPE atrophy with prominent choroidal vessels and mid-peripheral bone-spicule pigment mobilization. Full-field electroretinography demonstrated absent a- and b-waves in both dark- and light-adapted phases, and pattern ERG lacked a P50 wave. Axial lengths were 26.07 mm (right eye) and 26.13 mm (left eye). 

Thus, the patient presented with a syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy characterized electrophysiologically as rod–cone dysfunction with macular involvement, in the setting of high bilateral myopia, presenile cataracts, facial dysmorphism, transient childhood neutropenia, intellectual disability, truncal obesity, joint hyperextensibility, and microcephaly.
